alloy.preparation: Heat-treated at 1300°C for 58 h to homogenize concentration; machined as rods/rotating discs, 3.57-mm diameter (0.1 cm²). For potentiostatic surface-analysis experiments no epoxy insulation; meniscus contact prevents wetting the rod side. Mechanically polished with SiC and 1-µm alumina, washed with ethanol and doubly distilled water.
alloy.microstructure: Single-phase ferritic alloy; grains in the millimetre range after homogenization; a few chromium-oxide inclusions.

test_method.procedure_description: Rotating-disc electrode at 3000 rpm. Cathodic polarization at −650 mV for 1 min followed by an anodic hold for 1 h at 200 mV (PL) relative to normal hydrogen electrode. Solartron 1286/AMEL 568; current recorded versus time. Electrode removed with potential still applied, rinsed with doubly distilled water, dried/stored under argon for up to 2 h before surface analysis.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Pitting would produce a current increase associated with pit initiation/growth. Authors exclude pitting during PL and PH because no such current-transient increase is observed.

experiments.result_note: No-pitting lower limit from the authors’ explicit interpretation of current–time transients, not an onset digitized from polarization curves. Electrolyte A: 0.1 M H2SO4 + 0.4 M Na2SO4; B adds 0.12 M NaCl. Applies only to the stated hold; no claim of pitting at this potential. No-pitting interpretation applies to the one-hour hold; the paper separately reports pitting of Fe–24Cr in electrolyte B during broader polarization. Table 1 wt% values are retained; parenthesized at% values are not converted or mixed into the composition.
